(men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] | years16 = 2025–2026 | team16 = [[Kawasaki Brave Thunders]] | years17 = 2026–present | team17 = [[Trabzonspor B.K.|Trabzonspor]] | highlights = *[[Bevo Francis Award]] winner (2018) *First-team [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] – [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] (2018) *[[South Atlantic Conference|SAC]] Player of the Year (2018) *SAC Defensive Player of the Year (2018) *First-team All-SAC (2018) }} '''Emanuel Davon Terry''' (born August 21, 1996) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Trabzonspor B.K.|Trabzonspor]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[Basketball Champions League|FIBA Champions League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Lincoln Memorial Railsplitters|Lincoln Memorial Railsplitters]], earning [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors in 2018. ==College career== Terry, a 6’9 [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] from Cleveland High School in [[Cleveland, Alabama]], began his career as a reserve at Lincoln Memorial. He had a breakout season as a senior, averaging 16.9 points, 10.3 rebounds and 2.2 blocked shots per game. Terry led the Railsplitters to [[South Atlantic Conference]] (SAC) regular season and [[South Atlantic Conference men's basketball tournament|tournament]] championships. For the 2017–18 season, he was named the SAC Player of the Year and was the inaugural conference defensive player of the year.{{cite web |title=Emanuel Terry named finalist for 2018 Bevo Francis Award |url=https://m.middlesborodailynews.com/2018/04/02/emanuel-terry-named-finalist-for-2018-bevo-francis-award/ |website=[[Middlesboro Daily News]]|accessdate=August 12, 2018 |date=April 2, 2018}} On the national level, Terry was named an All-American by the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]].{{cite web |title=Terry headed to NBA Summer League |url=https://www.claiborneprogress.net/2018/07/03/terry-headed-to-nba-summer-league/ |website=Claiborne Progress|accessdate=August 12, 2018 |date=April 2, 2018}} He also won the [[Bevo Francis Award]] as the top small college player in the country.{{cite web |title=Emanuel Terry lauded with 2018 Bevo Francis Award |url=http://lmurailsplitters.com/news/2018/4/2/mens-basketball-emanuel-terry-lauded-with-2018-bevo-francis-award.aspx |website=LMURailsplitters.com|accessdate=August 12, 2018 |date=April 2, 2018}} ==Professional career== ===Canton Charge (2018–2019)=== After going undrafted in 2018, Terry was signed by the [[Denver Nuggets]] for their [[NBA Summer League]] team.{{cite web |title=LMU's Emanuel Terry turning heads at NBA Summer League |url=http://www.wymt.com/content/sports/LMUs-Emanuel-Terry-turning-heads-at-NBA-Summer-League-487686881.html |website=WYMT.com |accessdate=August 12, 2018 |date=July 9, 2018}}{{cite web |last = Dempsey | first = Christopher|title=Is Emanuel Terry the Next Torrey Craig? |url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/is-emanuel-terry-the-next-torrey-craig-070718-2 |website=NBA.com |accessdate=August 12, 2018 |date=July 7, 2018}} Following a strong showing there, he was signed by the Nuggets to compete for a roster spot on their training camp roster.{{cite web |title=Nuggets Sign Rookie DeVaughn Akoon-Purcell to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-akoon-purcell-080718 |website=NBA.com |accessdate=August 12, 2018 |date=August Emanuel Terry|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/terry-signing-181011|website=NBA.com|accessdate=October 11, 2018|date=October 11, 2018}} On October 13, he was waived by the Cavaliers.{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Waive Bonzie Colson, Kobi Simmons and Emanuel Terry|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/waive-colson-simmons-terry-181013|website=NBA.com|accessdate=October 16, 2018|date=October 13, 2018}} He was then added to the training camp roster for the Cavaliers’ [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Canton Charge]].{{cite web|title=Canton Charge 2018-19 Training Camp Roster|url=https://canton.gleague.nba.com/news/charge-2018-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 20, 2018|accessdate=October 21, 2018|archive-date=July 15, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200715165026/https://canton.gleague.nba.com/news/charge-2018-training-camp-roster/|url-status=dead}} Terry played 20 games for Canton, averaging 8.1 points and 6.4 rebounds for the team.{{cite news |last1=Boutwell |first1=Josh |title=Enterprise native continues to chase hoops dreams overseas |url=http://www.southeastsun.com/sports/article_4489811e-639d-11ea-b2e1-2f8745592302.html |accessdate=October 19, 2020 |work=Southeast Sun |date=March 11, 2020}} ===Sioux Falls Skyforce / Phoenix Suns / Miami Heat (2019)=== On January 5, 2019, Terry was traded to the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] for guard [[Malik Newman]].{{cite web|title=Skyforce acquire Emanuel Terry|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-acquire-emanuel-terry/|website=NBA.com|accessdate=January 5, 2019|date=January 5, 2019|archive-date=April 13, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190413122724/https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-acquire-emanuel-terry/|url-status=dead}} Since the trade, Terry improved upon his averages with Sioux Falls, averaging around 15.9 points, 8.1 rebounds, 1.6 assists, and 1.3 blocks per game in the seven games he played for them. On January 27, 2019, Terry signed a 10-day contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]]{{cite web|title=Phoenix Suns Sign Emanuel Terry|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/phoenix-suns-sign-emanuel-terry|website=NBA.com|accessdate=January 27, 2019|date=January 27, 2019}} and made his NBA debut the same day. That night, he recorded 5 points, 3 rebounds, 2 steals, and an assist in 8 minutes of play during a 116–102 loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/games/20190127/PHXLAL#/boxscore |title=Archived copy |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=January 28, 2019 |archive-date=January 28, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190128141850/https://www.nba.com/games/20190127/PHXLAL#/boxscore |url-status=dead }} He played in one other game with the Suns before the 10-day contract expired on February 7.{{cite web|title=Emanuel Terry: Contract expires|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/emanuel-terry-contract-expires/|date=February 7, 2019|website=cbssports.com|accessdate=February 7, 2019}} The next day, he was reacquired by Sioux Falls.{{cite web|title=SKYFORCE RE-ACQUIRES TERRY, LIGGINS|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-re-acquires-terry-liggins/|date=February 8, 2019|work=NBA.com|accessdate=February 8, 2019|archive-date=April 26, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190426161216/https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-re-acquires-terry-liggins/|url-status=dead}} On February 20, 2019, Terry signed a 10-day contract with the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|title=Heat Signs Emanuel Terry To 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-emanuel-terry-190220|website=NBA.com|accessdate=February 20, 2019|date=February 20, 2019}} He was re-acquired by the Skyforce afterwards.{{cite web|title=Emanuel Terry: Time with Miami |website=kkcrvenazvezda.rs|date=December 26, 2020 |accessdate=26 December 2020}} ===Agua Caliente Clippers (2021)=== For the 2020–21 season, Terry landed with the [[Agua Caliente Clippers]] of the G League, making his debut on February 11, 2021. He averaged 11 points, 10 rebounds, two assists and one block per game.{{cite news |last1=Boutwell |first1=Josh |title=Emanuel Terry turns in stellar G-League season |url=https://www.southeastsun.com/sports/article_3c44b084-8ca8-11eb-998a-9f2812845b88.html |access-date=October 16, 2021 |work=The Southeast Sun |date=March 24, 2021}} ===Stockton Kings / Return to the Phoenix Suns (2021–2022)=== In August 2021, Terry joined the [[Sacramento Kings]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=Kings Announce California Classic Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-announce-2021-ca-classic-roster|work=NBA.com|date=August 1, 2021|access-date=October 3, 2021}} On September 28, 2021, he signed a contract with the Kings.{{cite web|title=Kings Announce 2021-22 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-announce-2021-22-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=September 28, 2021|access-date=September 28, 2021}} Terry was waived on October 15{{cite web|title=Kings Waive Emanuel Terry|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-waive-emanuel-terry|website=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2021|access-date=October 16, 2021}} and joined the [[Stockton Kings]] later that month.{{cite web|title=Stockton Kings Announce 2021-22 Training Camp Roster|url=https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/stockton-kings-announce-2021-22-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 25, 2021|access-date=November 2, 2021}} On December 27, 2021, Terry signed a 10-day contract returning with the [[Phoenix Suns]] via the COVID-19 hardship waiver.{{cite news|title=Phoenix Suns add Emanuel Terry as hardship signing|url=https://arizonasports.com/story/2948383/phoenix-suns-add-emanuel-terry-as-hardship-signing/|work=Arizona Sports|date=December 27, 2021|access-date=December 27, 2021}} Terry played 3 games with the Suns in that contract, averaging 5 rebounds per game there, before being waived early from it. On January 4, 2022, he was reacquired and activated by Stockton.{{cite web|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 4, 2022}} ===Orléans Loiret Basket (2022)=== On April 9, 2022, Terry signed with [[Orléans Loiret Basket]] of the French [[LNB Pro A|Betclic Élite]].{{cite web|title=Emanuel Terry arrive en renfort (09/04/2022)|url=https://www.orleansloiretbasket.fr/Ress_10282/Club/Actualites-Communiques/Emanuel-Terry-arrive-en-renfort-.html|website=OrleansLoiretBasket.fr|date=April 9, 2022|access-date=April 9, 2022|language=French}} ===Seoul Samsung Thunders (2022–2023)=== On August 11, 2022, he has signed with [[Seoul Samsung Thunders]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]].{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/seoul-samsung-thunders-sign-marcus-derrickson-emanuel-terry/|title=Seoul Samsung Thunders sign Marcus Derrickson, Emanuel Terry|date=August 11, 2022|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 16, 2022|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }} ===Pallacanestro Trieste (2023)=== On January 17, 2023, he signed with [[Pallacanestro Trieste]] of the Italia [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/emanuel-terry-officially-signs-with-trieste/|title=Emanuel Terry officially signs with Trieste|date=January 17, 2023|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=January 17, 2023 |last1=Maggi |first1=Alessandro }} ===Manisa BB (2023–2024)=== On July 17, 2023, he signed with [[Manisa Büyükşehir Belediyespor|Manisa BB]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite web|url=https://manisabbsk.com.tr/33052/ailemize-hos-geldin-emanuel-terry.html|title=Ailemize Hoş Geldin Emanuel Terry|last=|first=|date=July 17, 2023|website=manisabbsk.com.tr|publisher=|language=tr|access-date=July 20, 2023}} ===Beşiktaş (2024–2025)=== On June 28, 2024, Terry signed with [[Beşiktaş J.K.
